articleSummary: As of June 24, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached alarming levels, with 1,094 confirmed cases and 277 deaths reported. Challenges such as misinformation, violence against health workers, and shortages of personal protective equipment (PPE) are hindering response efforts. articleSummary: As of June 23, 2026, Kerala has reported 159 confirmed dengue cases and one related death, amidst a total of 13,747 fever-related hospital visits this year. The state is facing a concerning increase in infectious diseases, including 15 new cases of Shigellosis and 22 cases of chickenpox. In response, the health department has launched the GOAL program to enhance outbreak control through improved sanitation and vector management, particularly with the monsoon season approaching. Authorities are urging the public to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and seek early medical intervention, especially for vulnerable populations such as pregnant women. The outbreak is characterized by diarrhea as a primary symptom, with transmission linked to contaminated water and food. Public health officials emphasize the need for increased awareness and preventive measures to mitigate the impact of these concurrent outbreaks, which also include cases of leptospirosis, jaundice, and malaria. The high-level epidemic-prevention committee has recommended a statewide three-month intensive drive for mosquito control and enhanced hygiene awareness.

articleHeadline: Nipah in India: Health authorities implement containment amid multiple outbreaks
articleSummary: As of June 23, 2026, Kerala is facing a critical situation with the Nipah virus, where one patient is on ventilator support at Kozhikode Medical College Hospital. Health officials have initiated containment measures, including an epidemic calendar, to manage overlapping outbreaks of Nipah, chikungunya, influenza, and measles. Currently, 93 individuals are under observation, with 11 low-risk contacts having completed their 21-day monitoring without symptoms. Investigations into the infection's source are ongoing, with negative results from local fruit bats and domestic animals. No community spread has been reported, but health authorities are enhancing surveillance and public awareness.
